## Design

### 2026-10-09 – current progress:

**3.12h**

current progress:
-   made the schematic
-   started routing the pcb
Since i am not used to hardware or pcb making, it took me a long while to understand how the program worked but i soon got used to how it worked.

I worked in easy EDA as i didn't want to download Kicad but i'm pretty sure it works the same with correct dimentions.
Luckily after a quick bit of exploration I realized I could download the care package through easyEDA's own inbuilt import kiCAD system so i have the exact same footprints as in the package.

First i just got the parts down and then worked out how, where , etc.*  and then i  attached the net labels where they were supposed to be placed.When after i finished than , i went to attach  footprints (a bit intimidating at first) and converted to pcb.

After trying a few different designs i made a cat to symbolise a pet (not exactly a 'star' bie but oh-well.)
I adjusted the parts and started trying to connect.  Not very neat though

*One part that took particularly long was to find the  correct item and parts through the system. It took me some time to find where that option was for the parts i couldn't find (I had to scroll down).

Some errors i got into were that i didn't attach the correct footprint or at least not the specified one on the guide. I only had done a bit of work on the pcb side so it wasn't too disastrous.

A small modification i used is that instead of a 4pin, i used a 3 pin DHT11 sensor footprint pin as  the sensor I was looking at had only 3 pins so i thought it best to use 3.
